title: Grammar-Growing Certificates — proposal
subfield: Proof embryology: certificates that develop new expressive power
open: A descendant introduces new predicates, types, or inference rules, but must supply a translation showing that claims in the old vocabulary have not acquired unjustified new proofs.
status: The missing ingredient is an efficient extension-certificate language that permits useful invention while excluding disguised new axioms.
why: Verification ecosystems that invent domain-specific concepts without periodically replacing their foundational trust.
key_works: Proof-carrying data and foundational approaches to proof-carrying code.

title: Theorem-Compiler Seeds — proposal
subfield: Proof embryology: certificates that develop new expressive power
open: From a certified theorem family, a seed produces a descendant prover and verifier whose accepted outputs remain inside that family’s authorized consequences.
status: Specialization must preserve soundness while allowing cost to follow the specialized computation rather than the entire original interpreter.
why: Research programs that manufacture increasingly efficient verification machinery as their theories develop.
key_works: SuperNova’s nonuniform incremental verification and CompCert’s semantic-preservation methodology.

title: Challenge-Morphing Proofs — proposal
subfield: Proof embryology: certificates that develop new expressive power
open: An adversarial verifier adaptively requests stronger properties of one committed object. Every response must be jointly consistent with that object while hiding unrequested properties.
status: The research target is compact, adaptively secure consistency across changing relations, including selective abort and correlated disclosures.
why: Interactive audits that deepen organically instead of requiring a complete specification before the first certificate.
key_works: Function-hiding functional commitments.

title: Latent Lemma Pods — proposal
subfield: Proof embryology: certificates that develop new expressive power
open: Each pod binds a hidden lemma, its derivation, and an activation predicate. Awakening releases only the authorized lemma and proves its connection to the original theorem.
status: Adaptive activation must not leak dormant lemmas through rejection behavior or permit stale evidence to awaken them.
why: Scientific and institutional certificates that disclose deeper justification only during disputes, emergencies, or later research.
key_works: Functional encryption and proof-carrying data.

title: Proof-Generated Witness Markets — proposal
subfield: Proof embryology: certificates that develop new expressive power
open: A parent emits subproblems, acceptance relations, and escrowed rewards, with a certificate that accepted solutions discharge specified parent obligations.
status: The missing theory must prevent circular rewards, duplicated obligations, and generators that manufacture easy but irrelevant work.
why: Autonomous theorem, audit, and scientific-discovery economies in which useful results generate their own next-stage demand.
key_works: Proof-carrying data and Zerocash-style private value conservation.

title: Ancestry-Oblivious Proof Growth — proposal
subfield: Proof embryology: certificates that develop new expressive power
open: Histories with identical declared outputs and leakage must remain indistinguishable, even when they differ in branching, merging, rejected attempts, and internal participants.
status: Hiding proof contents is insufficient; proof size, update timing, and graph access patterns also require treatment.
why: Private research organizations and negotiation networks that reveal conclusions without exposing their internal structure.
key_works: Dynamic ZK accumulators and Path ORAM.

title: Semantic Proof Pruning — proposal
subfield: Proof embryology: certificates that develop new expressive power
open: A pruning step replaces history \(H\) with summary \(S\), accompanied by a certificate that every query in an admitted class has the same answer on both.
status: Useful query-preserving summaries are domain-specific; arbitrary unforeseen questions cannot be supported by magical lossless compression.
why: Long-lived proof organisms whose storage does not grow in proportion to every event they have experienced.
key_works: Functional commitments and provenance algebra.

title: Coinductive Service Oaths — proposal
subfield: Proof embryology: certificates that develop new expressive power
open: A service carries an invariant and a progress argument establishing ongoing obligations under explicit scheduling, funding, and availability assumptions.
status: A finite execution proof cannot establish unconditional future service; the missing package must expose and preserve its environmental assumptions.
why: Persistent autonomous services whose promises concern continued operation, not merely correct isolated responses.
key_works: Concurrent program logics and proof-carrying data.

title: Autocatalytic Patch Vaults — proposal
subfield: Concealed mutation: programs that generate and hide their own repairs
open: A hostile host observes successive executables, but each accepted successor proves that a committed internal mutation process obeyed inherited behavior and disclosure constraints.
status: The missing theorem concerns adaptive, correlated generations—not merely the security of one obfuscated program.
why: Confidential autonomous software that improves without exposing its source to a maintainer.
key_works: *Cryptography with Updates* and iO constructions.

title: Patch-Existence Hiding — proposal
subfield: Concealed mutation: programs that generate and hide their own repairs
open: Real updates and certified dummy updates are indistinguishable whenever their permitted observable behavior and declared resource leakage agree.
status: Update privacy must cover binary structure, traffic, runtime, and state migration—not just encrypted patch bytes.
why: Maintenance that does not advertise vulnerability discoveries, internal experiments, or strategic changes.
key_works: Updatable randomized encodings and update-hiding accumulators.

title: Sealed-Patch Courtship — proposal
subfield: Concealed mutation: programs that generate and hide their own repairs
open: Contributors submit hidden transformations; a committed selection process chooses an admissible winner without exposing losing patches or the recipient program.
status: Candidate evaluation can leak the target program, and repeated competitions can leak losing intellectual property.
why: Collaborative improvement markets for software that no single contributor may inspect.
key_works: Updatable cryptography and function-hiding commitments.

title: Epigenetic Interface Switching — proposal
subfield: Concealed mutation: programs that generate and hide their own repairs
open: An environmental credential activates an interface-generation rule, but cannot confer authority beyond the program’s inherited policy.
status: The missing composition rule must constrain both newly generated interfaces and information leaked by repeated environment switching.
why: Private software that adapts its capabilities to communities, devices, and institutions without distributing unrelated versions.
key_works: Macaroons’ contextual delegation and functional encryption.

title: Causal-Delta Cloaks — proposal
subfield: Concealed mutation: programs that generate and hide their own repairs
open: Two old–new program pairs are indistinguishable when their admitted interactions reveal the same semantic change and permitted leakage.
status: This needs a related-program, multiversion security definition; ordinary iO alone does not establish it.
why: Auditable private upgrades whose externally meaningful change is inspectable without revealing the repair.
key_works: iO and updatable cryptography.

title: Repair-Reproduction Firewalls — proposal
subfield: Concealed mutation: programs that generate and hide their own repairs
open: Every generated helper receives a derived capability and a checked task contract; helpers cannot reconstruct broader authority by colluding.
status: Attenuation must compose across helper interactions, shared secrets, and semantic effects—not merely individual API permissions.
why: Self-maintaining software populations that can delegate deeply without creating an expanding administrator class.
key_works: Macaroons and proof-carrying code.

title: Key-Reborn Successors — proposal
subfield: Concealed mutation: programs that generate and hide their own repairs
open: After a certified refresh involving sufficient honest fresh entropy, possession of all pre-refresh program state does not reveal the successor’s protected future secrets.
status: The required theorem must combine compromise recovery with hidden program evolution and inherited capabilities.
why: Autonomous recovery that changes the security future instead of merely replacing vulnerable code.
key_works: Dynamic proactive secret sharing.

title: Quarantined Mutation Chambers — proposal
subfield: Concealed mutation: programs that generate and hide their own repairs
open: Candidate execution occurs inside a sealed chamber whose outputs follow a fixed disclosure policy, including failed tests and rejection decisions.
status: Even a score or acceptance bit can encode secrets; the chamber needs adaptive leakage bounds.
why: Exploratory self-modification without treating every experimental patch as trusted production code.
key_works: FHE and fully adaptive privacy composition.

title: Polycentric Organisms — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic organisms: bodies, development, injury, sterility, death
open: Different committees control distinct secret states and capabilities; organism-level actions require certified coordination among the relevant organs.
status: Organ replacement and cross-organ failures need a composition theorem that does not secretly reintroduce a universal recovery key.
why: Autonomous entities whose internal checks and balances remain enforceable after deployment.
key_works: Universally composable protocols and dynamic secret sharing.

title: Ontogenetic Quorums — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic organisms: bodies, development, injury, sterility, death
open: Committee size, access structure, and recovery rules evolve through certified transitions that preserve a declared adversary model.
status: Adding identities does not prove additional honesty; the model must specify enrollment assumptions and cross-generation corruption limits.
why: Small organisms that can grow into large distributed institutions without replacing their identity or losing their secrets.
key_works: Dynamic-committee proactive secret sharing.

title: Wound-Limited Regeneration — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic organisms: bodies, development, injury, sterility, death
open: A recovery identifies compromised compartments, revokes their future authority, and certifies which unaffected state and guarantees remain valid.
status: Recovery must account for secrets already learned and capabilities already exercised; regeneration cannot undo those facts.
why: Recoverable autonomous systems that neither restart from nothing nor pretend compromise never occurred.
key_works: Proactive sharing and composable security models.

title: Metamorphic Selfhood — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic organisms: bodies, development, injury, sterility, death
open: Identity continuity is a certified relation over selected obligations and state projections, rather than equality of keys or binaries.
status: The identity relation must be explicit enough to prevent arbitrary replacement while allowing meaningful transformation.
why: Persistent agents and institutions that can genuinely transform without abandoning accountability.
key_works: Proof-carrying data and contextual refinement methods.

title: Senescence Without Sovereigns — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic organisms: bodies, development, injury, sterility, death
open: Capabilities decay across authenticated epochs unless a precommitted renewal condition is satisfied; descendants inherit the same renewal restrictions.
status: Epoch availability, emergency operation, and renewal evidence must be modeled without granting an unrestricted override.
why: Delegations that cannot become permanent merely through controller inertia.
key_works: Contextual capability restrictions and cryptographic timestamping.

title: Sterile-but-Living Programs — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic organisms: bodies, development, injury, sterility, death
open: A sterilization transition consumes every recognized birth capability but preserves specified execution rights; existing copies cannot obtain new certified descendants.
status: Every recognized reproduction route, including delegation and migration, must honor the sterilization boundary.
why: Controlled deployment of useful self-reproducing systems without requiring their destruction.
key_works: Private spend prevention and attenuated authorization.

title: Cryptographic Organ Donation — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic organisms: bodies, development, injury, sterility, death
open: A donor delegates or transfers a specified functional capability, with explicit rules for whether its own corresponding authority survives.
status: Functional inheritance must remain secure under donor–recipient collusion and repeated extraction of overlapping “organs.”
why: Reuse of private expertise, archives, and service modules across independently governed organisms.
key_works: Functional and mergeable functional encryption.

title: Posthumous Duty Engines — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic organisms: bodies, development, injury, sterility, death
open: Death disables general action, but activates a finite executor authorized only to discharge committed obligations using reserved resources.
status: The executor must not become a disguised continuation of the deceased organism’s unrestricted authority.
why: Autonomous systems that can terminate without abandoning customers, counterparties, or shared infrastructure.
key_works: Capability attenuation and resource-accounting program logics.

title: Proof-Carrying Semantic Deltas — proposal
subfield: Proof-carrying software evolution
open: A patch certificate specifies where old and new behavior may differ and proves preservation outside that region under an explicit execution model.
status: The efficiency target is proof generation proportional to the affected dependency region, not the whole application.
why: Upgrades that are auditable as changes rather than repeatedly audited from scratch.
key_works: CompCert and ReLoC.

title: Rollback Without Resurrection — proposal
subfield: Proof-carrying software evolution
open: A rollback preserves a monotone external-effect history while restoring only reversible state; every resumed action is checked against that history.
status: Participating external services must expose durable admission and completion semantics.
why: Safe recovery for autonomous agents that have already sent messages, moved resources, or changed external systems.
key_works: RIFL’s exactly-once RPC machinery and private spend prevention.

title: Live-Upgrade Bisimulation — proposal
subfield: Proof-carrying software evolution
open: Mixed-version executions must simulate an admitted abstract service, including concurrent requests and partially migrated state.
status: The hard case is interference between old readers, new writers, and operations already in flight.
why: Continuous evolution without requiring global shutdowns or trusting ad hoc compatibility logic.
key_works: Iris and ReLoC’s concurrent refinement reasoning.

title: Contract-Discovering Descendants — proposal
subfield: Proof-carrying software evolution
open: An inferred contract becomes authoritative only after a checked proof under the declared program semantics; observations alone cannot promote it to a universal guarantee.
status: Useful invariant discovery must avoid trivial guarantees and must distinguish inferred intent from proved behavior.
why: Systems whose formal understanding of themselves improves after deployment.
key_works: Proof-carrying code and foundational verification.

title: Noninterfering Test Offspring — proposal
subfield: Proof-carrying software evolution
open: Generated tests must follow a certified coverage generator, while their oracles and protected evaluation inputs remain outside the patch’s influence.
status: Test generation, oracle generation, and selection feedback require separate information-flow guarantees.
why: Autonomous development that grows its test suite without rewarding self-serving tests.
key_works: Authenticated build processes and adaptive evaluation methods.

title: Dependency-Boundary Shrinkage — proposal
subfield: Proof-carrying software evolution
open: A successor replaces specified trust assumptions with checked implementations or proofs, while exposing any new assumptions introduced elsewhere.
status: Trust dependencies include compilers, deployment machinery, configuration, and external services—not only imported libraries.
why: Software that becomes more independently verifiable as it evolves.
key_works: CompCert and in-toto.

title: Environment-True Repair Capsules — proposal
subfield: Proof-carrying software evolution
open: The certificate binds the repair to committed permissions, files, dependencies, pending actions, and available tools—not a retrospectively cleaned environment.
status: External nondeterminism and incomplete capture require explicit boundaries rather than a claim of perfect replay.
why: Credible autonomous incident response and repair-learning datasets without hidden environmental substitutions.
key_works: in-toto’s process provenance and verifiable stateful execution.

title: Protocol Molting — proposal
subfield: Proof-carrying software evolution
open: An accepted molt preserves specified guarantees across enrolled old and new clients, including messages created before activation but delivered afterward.
status: Cross-version authentication and delayed authority are not solved merely by proving each version separately.
why: Long-lived protocols that can change fundamentally without treating delayed traffic as an exceptional afterthought.
key_works: Composable security and relational program verification.

title: Optimizer-Complete Bloodlines — proposal
subfield: Learning bloodlines: models that generate accountable descendants
open: Every accepted update binds weights, optimizer accumulators, data ordering, randomness, learning-rate state, and restart decisions to its committed parent.
status: The target is efficient proof of the complete update state, including mixed-precision and implementation-specific behavior.
why: Fine-tuning lineages that remain meaningful across pauses, migrations, and distributed training.
key_works: Recursive zero-knowledge proofs of training.

title: Causal Fine-Tuning Twins — proposal
subfield: Learning bloodlines: models that generate accountable descendants
open: Two certified training runs share their prescribed initialization and randomness but differ in one declared intervention, such as an added dataset.
status: This establishes algorithmic counterfactuals under the specified experiment, not unrestricted causal claims about real-world usefulness.
why: Private, reproducible attribution of model changes to particular learning decisions.
key_works: Proofs of training and verifiable unlearning.

title: Synthetic-Data Inheritance Rules — proposal
subfield: Learning bloodlines: models that generate accountable descendants
open: Enrolled synthetic examples inherit provenance and permitted-use predicates; transformations cannot remove those predicates merely by changing representation.
status: The guarantee requires mediated lineage admission; cryptography cannot detect every externally reintroduced paraphrase.
why: Model ecosystems in which distillation and synthetic data do not automatically erase consent or privacy accounting.
key_works: Proof-carrying data and adaptive privacy composition.

title: Learner-Reachable Teaching — proposal
subfield: Learning bloodlines: models that generate accountable descendants
open: A teaching artifact includes a certified action sequence from the learner’s committed state using only its available tools and permissions.
status: Reachability does not prove the teacher lacked hindsight; that separate information boundary must remain explicit.
why: Distillation from successful repairs without teaching impossible jumps through missing files, privileges, or infrastructure.
key_works: Stateful verifiable computation and process provenance.

title: Evaluation-Quarantined Germlines — proposal
subfield: Learning bloodlines: models that generate accountable descendants
open: Every descendant carries the cumulative allowed information obtained from protected evaluators, including scores, selection outcomes, and rejected experiments.
status: Complete mediation is difficult, and a newly enrolled ancestor may already contain unaccounted external information.
why: Self-improvement experiments whose reported progress remains interpretable across generations.
key_works: Reusable holdouts and fully adaptive privacy accounting.

title: Counterfactual Erasure Branches — proposal
subfield: Learning bloodlines: models that generate accountable descendants
open: The system constructs descendants consistent with a specified removal procedure, then proves permitted comparisons between actual and erased branches.
status: Correct execution of an unlearning algorithm must not be confused with a stronger distributional erasure guarantee it lacks.
why: Auditable decisions about deletion, retention, and downstream replacement without immediately exposing or deploying every candidate.
key_works: Cryptographically verifiable machine unlearning.

title: Encrypted Skill Budding — proposal
subfield: Learning bloodlines: models that generate accountable descendants
open: A child is produced by an approved extraction or distillation procedure and receives a restricted interface plus inherited disclosure constraints.
status: Behavioral specialization alone does not establish reduced information leakage; the restriction needs its own security definition.
why: Markets for narrowly scoped machine expertise without transferring complete parent models.
key_works: Proofs of training and functional encryption.

title: Self-Updating Inference Receipts — proposal
subfield: Learning bloodlines: models that generate accountable descendants
open: Each response binds to an authenticated sequence of inference and authorized update steps, preventing silent substitution of another checkpoint or hidden adaptation.
status: Proof cost and state synchronization must remain manageable when inference and learning interleave at fine granularity.
why: Continually learning agents whose individual outputs retain inspectable lineage.
key_works: Recursive training proofs and modular zkML proof construction.

title: Objective-Breeding Constitutions — proposal
subfield: Evolving institutions: rules that generate rules under accountable selection
open: A new objective must satisfy certified transformation rules and preserve a separately anchored set of constraints.
status: The objective-change rules themselves require legitimate specification; cryptography cannot determine which values deserve protection.
why: Institutions that can learn what to optimize without silently abandoning their original commitments.
key_works: Function-hiding commitments and proof-carrying data.

title: Private-Regret Mandates — proposal
subfield: Evolving institutions: rules that generate rules under accountable selection
open: A mandate carries a certified cumulative-regret calculation over authenticated losses and a preregistered comparator family.
status: The missing package must bind every relevant round and distinguish formal regret from real-world welfare.
why: Adaptive delegation evaluated against explicit alternatives rather than favorable anecdotes.
key_works: Verifiable stateful computation and authenticated derived computations.

title: Experiment-Born Charters — proposal
subfield: Evolving institutions: rules that generate rules under accountable selection
open: A daughter institution receives authority only through a precommitted selection rule applied to authenticated trial evidence, with protected participants’ constraints preserved.
status: Trial validity depends on actual enrollment and measurement assumptions, not merely correct execution of the scoring circuit.
why: Institutional development through bounded experimentation rather than irreversible system-wide replacement.
key_works: Adaptive data-analysis methods and attenuated capabilities.

title: Mutation-Proof Exit Rights — proposal
subfield: Evolving institutions: rules that generate rules under accountable selection
open: Every amendment must preserve a funded, executable exit strategy under a specified failure and adversary model.
status: Exit guarantees must include data access, settlement, and availability—not merely an “exit” function in source code.
why: Deep cooperation among parties unwilling to trust future institutional leadership.
key_works: Composable protocol guarantees and resource-sensitive verification.

title: Generation-Spanning Conflict Checks — proposal
subfield: Evolving institutions: rules that generate rules under accountable selection
open: A selection proof checks candidate, evaluator, and beneficiary relationships across an authenticated succession graph while concealing irrelevant identities.
status: The guarantee is only as complete as the enrolled control graph; hidden real-world ownership is not cryptographically observable.
why: Private institutional experimentation with auditable restrictions on self-dealing.
key_works: ZK set operations and distributed graph certification.

title: Dissent-Generating Amendments — proposal
subfield: Evolving institutions: rules that generate rules under accountable selection
open: An amendment certificate includes the strongest violations it causes within a committed finite objection language, or proofs that no such violations exist.
status: The objection language must be useful and explicit; completeness cannot mean “every objection anyone could imagine.”
why: Governance proposals that arrive with authenticated adversarial analysis rather than selectively chosen supporting arguments.
key_works: Functional commitments and verifiable computation.

title: Private Bargain Germination — proposal
subfield: Evolving institutions: rules that generate rules under accountable selection
open: A new rule is accepted only if it improves or preserves every enrolled party’s committed utility according to the negotiated criterion.
status: Adaptive bargaining leaks preferences, and strategic preference reports remain a mechanism-design issue.
why: Repeated institutional renegotiation without public disclosure of reservation values.
key_works: Secure computation and function-hiding commitments.

title: Two-Speed Constitutional Metabolism — proposal
subfield: Evolving institutions: rules that generate rules under accountable selection
open: Every mutation is typed as operational or constitutional, with proofs that operational changes cannot simulate forbidden constitutional effects.
status: Syntactic classification is insufficient; a seemingly ordinary rule can indirectly change who controls resources.
why: Adaptable institutions without an emergency loophole that gradually becomes unrestricted sovereignty.
key_works: Proof-carrying code and contextual authorization.

title: Theorem-Fertile Myths — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic myths: authenticated claims that generate further worlds
open: Descendant statements derive from the parent’s canonical semantic output and a certified generator, not from arbitrary proof encodings that a prover can manipulate.
status: The generator must create meaningful obligations while preventing circular endorsement and uncontrolled assumption growth.
why: Self-expanding formal traditions, simulations, and collective narratives.
key_works: Proof-carrying data and authenticated derived computation.

title: Unpaid-Lemma Mythologies — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic myths: authenticated claims that generate further worlds
open: Every descendant carries an authenticated set of undischarged assumptions; no transformation can relabel a conditional conclusion as unconditional without the required proofs.
status: Dependency compression must preserve logical obligations even when alternative derivations and shared assumptions appear.
why: Speculative scientific and cultural systems that distinguish fertile conjecture from established consequence.
key_works: Provenance semirings and ZK accumulators.

title: Paraconsistent Cryptographic Worlds — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic myths: authenticated claims that generate further worlds
open: Claims carry explicit logical contexts, and cross-context derivations use a checked non-explosive calculus with specified export rules.
status: The cryptography is not the difficult philosophy; the research target is useful, composable context-export rules.
why: Shared computational institutions among communities with incompatible assumptions.
key_works: PCD-based enforcement of language semantics.

title: Ritual Role Genesis — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic myths: authenticated claims that generate further worlds
open: A digital process generates a role schema and its initial holders, with a proof that the new role’s authority follows from the participants’ existing capabilities.
status: Role invention must not become authority invention; colluding participants cannot delegate powers they never possessed.
why: Communities that invent offices, memberships, and shared responsibilities without a permanent central registrar.
key_works: Contextual credentials and authenticated process provenance.

title: Metaphor Transport Proofs — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic myths: authenticated claims that generate further worlds
open: A transformation preserves declared structural predicates—such as dependency, obligation, or role correspondence—while labeling unsupported semantic interpretations.
status: Human meaning exceeds the formal predicates; the certificate must make that boundary visible.
why: Translation between cultural, institutional, and machine-readable worlds without claiming universal semantic equivalence.
key_works: Homomorphic signatures and provenance algebra.

title: Secret-Origin Canons — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic myths: authenticated claims that generate further worlds
open: Each canonical descendant proves ancestry from an authorized root set and compliance with inheritance rules, revealing only selected origin predicates.
status: Repeated ancestry queries can jointly reveal origins, especially when descendants merge.
why: Durable knowledge traditions whose vulnerable founders need not be exposed.
key_works: ZK accumulators and proof-carrying data.

title: Canonical Miracle Generators — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic myths: authenticated claims that generate further worlds
open: A precommitted stochastic process and rarity predicate determine which events count; every admitted event proves its position in the enrolled sampling history.
status: Hidden reruns and selective abort can manufacture apparent miracles unless enrollment and randomness are controlled.
why: Verifiable surprise as a generative ingredient in games, ceremonies, science, and collective storytelling.
key_works: Functional commitments and cryptographic timestamping.

title: Hereditary Interpretation Windows — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic myths: authenticated claims that generate further worlds
open: An author commits to content and an interpretation grammar; descendants may produce new formal readings only with certificates of admissibility.
status: The interpretation grammar must constrain semantic use, not merely accept any syntactic paraphrase.
why: Open-ended narratives and agreements that permit development without allowing arbitrary retrospective endorsement.
key_works: Homomorphic signatures and function-hiding commitments.

title: Causal Memorial Crystals — proposal
subfield: Memorial cryptography: memories that grow without falsifying their ancestry
open: A memorial authenticates message-level causal ancestry and permits selective proofs of ordering, dependence, and concurrency without exposing unrelated events.
status: Authenticated causal references establish recorded process dependence, not the ultimate truth of every reported event.
why: Archives that explain how an outcome arose without publishing every participant’s history.
key_works: Provenance semirings and distributed ZK graph certification.

title: Query-Born Memories — proposal
subfield: Memorial cryptography: memories that grow without falsifying their ancestry
open: Every derived answer becomes an archive object carrying its source dependencies, transformation rule, and remaining disclosure restrictions.
status: Repeated reuse and recombination must account for information revealed by the entire answer family.
why: Collective knowledge that grows through use without losing the distinction between original testimony and derived inference.
key_works: Provenance algebra and adaptive privacy filters.

title: Re-examinable Memory Fossils — proposal
subfield: Memorial cryptography: memories that grow without falsifying their ancestry
open: The fossil commits to an archived corpus and its custody guarantees, allowing later authenticated queries without pretending the commitment itself stores all evidence.
status: Long-term retrievability and future-query privacy must survive custodian turnover and changing cryptographic assumptions.
why: Small, portable memorials that can support investigations not anticipated by their first summarizers.
key_works: Compact proofs of retrievability and functional encryption.

title: Consent-Aging Archives — proposal
subfield: Memorial cryptography: memories that grow without falsifying their ancestry
open: Access policies evolve through authenticated consent and succession rules, while earlier public disclosures remain explicitly irreversible.
status: Conflicting consent, absent participants, and inherited authority require an explicit policy calculus.
why: Archives that can move between secrecy, collective use, and eventual disclosure without a permanent omnipotent custodian.
key_works: Functional encryption and attenuated authorization.

title: Memorial Recombination — proposal
subfield: Memorial cryptography: memories that grow without falsifying their ancestry
open: A merged memorial proves the agreed identity relation between overlapping records and preserves source-specific claims and contradictions.
status: Record identity is often uncertain; approximate matching must not be silently treated as exact historical identity.
why: Collective memory across communities that cannot simply pool their archives.
key_works: ZK authenticated set operations and provenance semirings.

title: Countermemory Challenges — proposal
subfield: Memorial cryptography: memories that grow without falsifying their ancestry
open: A challenge proves that authenticated evidence contradicts a specified formal claim, producing a persistent dispute object until reconciliation or qualified revision.
status: The contradiction relation must be explicit; conflicting accounts are not automatically proof that one is false.
why: Correctable public memory without requiring whistleblowers to publish everything they know.
key_works: ZK set proofs and proof-carrying data.

title: Anonymous Ancestral Credit — proposal
subfield: Memorial cryptography: memories that grow without falsifying their ancestry
open: A committed credit rule distributes a conserved reward across admitted ancestry, preventing repeated derivation paths from multiplying the same entitlement.
status: Procedural contribution is not identical to intellectual authorship; the credit rule must state what it actually measures.
why: Memory commons that preserve attribution and compensation without requiring public personal histories.
key_works: Provenance semirings and Zerocash.

title: Memory-Generated Investigations — proposal
subfield: Memorial cryptography: memories that grow without falsifying their ancestry
open: A certified generator turns missing fields, contradictions, or unsupported dependencies into new evidence requests, preserving a committed coverage policy.
status: The system needs nontrivial gap definitions and defenses against repeatedly investigating convenient questions.
why: Collective memories that actively improve rather than merely accumulate.
key_works: Provenance analysis and proof-carrying data.

title: Purpose-Blind Dream Foundries — proposal
subfield: Dream protocols: results before interpretation
open: A hidden purpose program is selected under multiparty secrecy, evaluated, and bound to a result commitment before its permitted disclosure.
status: Runtime, circuit shape, inputs, and selective abort can reveal the purpose unless included in the leakage model.
why: Audits and decisions that executors cannot tailor to a known purpose.
key_works: FHE and function-hiding commitments.

title: Space Commitments — proposal
subfield: Dream protocols: results before interpretation
open: A committed representation binds every supported answer, with a precise tradeoff between preprocessing, representation size, and later query work.
status: Arbitrary future questions cannot all receive cheap answers from a tiny representation; the supported family must be explicit.
why: Scientific and institutional computation prepared for purposes that emerge later.
key_works: Functional commitments and functional encryption.

title: Encrypted Counterfactual Sleep — proposal
subfield: Dream protocols: results before interpretation
open: A committed scenario family is evaluated privately; later authenticated evidence selects which result may be disclosed.
status: Scenario explosion and correlations between opened branches require explicit efficiency and disclosure limits.
why: Contingency systems that prepare before events occur without revealing every strategy.
key_works: FHE and recursive stateful computation.

title: Dream-to-Purpose Selection — proposal
subfield: Dream protocols: results before interpretation
open: After committing result \(y\), the system applies a previously committed generator \(G\) to produce purpose \(q=G(y)\), then proves both chronology and faithful generation.
status: The purpose itself may disclose sensitive properties of \(y\); purpose generation needs its own leakage contract.
why: Research and planning systems whose questions emerge from discoveries without retrospective manipulation.
key_works: Function-hiding commitments and proof-carrying data.

title: Failed-Awakening Privacy — proposal
subfield: Dream protocols: results before interpretation
open: Accepted and rejected query transcripts reveal only a specified response class, including whatever acceptance information the policy necessarily exposes.
status: Rejection bits can reconstruct hidden policy or data; a meaningful guarantee must quantify that channel rather than ignore it.
why: Sensitive computation that can safely face exploratory future-purpose requests.
key_works: Functional-encryption security definitions and adaptive privacy accounting.

title: Mutually Uninterpretable Dreams — proposal
subfield: Dream protocols: results before interpretation
open: Each custodian holds a protected result share; only an authorized joint purpose reveals the permitted function of their combination.
status: Repeated coalition changes and overlapping interpretations require adaptive collusion security.
why: Collaborations whose participants prepare useful work before knowing their eventual partners or application.
key_works: Mergeable functional encryption.

title: Delayed-Meaning Signatures — proposal
subfield: Dream protocols: results before interpretation
open: Future statements receive valid derived signatures only through an authenticated interpretation language, with context restrictions preserved.
status: Unrestricted derivability can create unintended endorsements; the interpretation policy must constrain both content and context.
why: Preauthorized scientific results, contingent agreements, and machine-generated attestations with bounded future meanings.
key_works: Homomorphic signatures.

title: Dream Compost — proposal
subfield: Dream protocols: results before interpretation
open: A transformation extracts approved reusable structure from sealed results while carrying forward their disclosure and provenance constraints.
status: Reuse can expose information that no original purpose was permitted to reveal; permissions must compose across transformation chains.
why: Economies of reusable private precomputation and research that compounds across abandoned purposes.
key_works: FHE, functional encryption, and adaptive privacy filters.

title: Proof-Certified Tissues — proposal
subfield: Spatial morphogenesis: cryptographic tissues and growing networks
open: Each admitted node or edge carries evidence that the enlarged authenticated graph satisfies selected connectivity, separation, or resource invariants.
status: The research target is local update cost and privacy across growth, not merely proving a static graph property.
why: Self-assembling distributed infrastructure without a trusted observer of the whole network.
key_works: Distributed noninteractive zero-knowledge proofs.

title: Secret Circulation Networks — proposal
subfield: Spatial morphogenesis: cryptographic tissues and growing networks
open: Routing and resharing may change where information resides, but unauthorized coalitions cannot accumulate enough compatible state to reconstruct it.
status: Security must account for adversaries collecting shares at different places and times.
why: Private computation that follows available infrastructure instead of remaining tied to one fixed committee.
key_works: Dynamic proactive secret sharing.

title: Time-Expanded Cut Security — proposal
subfield: Spatial morphogenesis: cryptographic tissues and growing networks
open: For a restricted linear sharing protocol, a certificate bounds the information obtainable from corrupted vertices in a time-expanded transfer graph.
status: Static graph cuts are insufficient; the missing theorem must account for correlated shares and adaptive corruption.
why: Auditable secrecy guarantees for migrating, branching, and recombining secret state.
key_works: Proactive sharing and distributed graph-proof techniques.

title: Shape-Bound Reproduction — proposal
subfield: Spatial morphogenesis: cryptographic tissues and growing networks
open: Birth must satisfy graph-relative constraints such as bounded degree, separation from conflicting roles, or attachment to an approved neighborhood.
status: Logical topology is not physical geography; any physical-location claim needs a separate attestation model.
why: Structured autonomous populations that cannot evade organizational constraints merely by spawning new identities.
key_works: Distributed ZK graph certification and private spend prevention.

title: Topology-Private Development — proposal
subfield: Spatial morphogenesis: cryptographic tissues and growing networks
open: Development histories with identical allowed outputs and capacity leakage remain indistinguishable to the specified observer.
status: Hiding graph data does not hide network traffic; the construction needs an explicit observer and communication model.
why: Private coalitions and research networks whose expansion does not expose their strategy.
key_works: Path ORAM and distributed ZK certification.

title: Boundary-Migrating Committees — proposal
subfield: Spatial morphogenesis: cryptographic tissues and growing networks
open: A migration provides an atomic authority transition even when state transfer overlaps and messages are delayed.
status: Share-transfer correctness and authority-transfer atomicity are different properties and must be proved together.
why: Mobile cryptographic institutions that can change their operators without duplicating control.
key_works: Dynamic secret sharing and composable key-management models.

title: Proof-Carrying Organogenesis — proposal
subfield: Spatial morphogenesis: cryptographic tissues and growing networks
open: A generated component must satisfy an interface contract and fit the global authority, privacy, and resource constraints of the existing system.
status: Generated components must compose semantically; separate proofs of local correctness do not establish safe interaction.
why: Infrastructure that develops new services rather than merely scaling replicas of old ones.
key_works: Proof-carrying code and universally composable security.

title: Metabolic Routing Proofs — proposal
subfield: Spatial morphogenesis: cryptographic tissues and growing networks
open: Accepted outputs carry certified processing ancestry, including required validation, consent, sanitization, or aggregation stages.
status: The guarantee concerns authenticated protocol stages; it cannot infer unobservable physical processing from a signature alone.
why: Self-organizing processing networks that cannot silently skip inconvenient obligations.
key_works: Proof-carrying data and in-toto.

title: Entitlement-Conserving Quantum Mitosis — proposal
subfield: Quantum developmental cryptography
open: A birth protocol consumes a valid parent entitlement and sufficient reproductive budget before an issuer creates children; it does not clone an unknown quantum state.
status: Issuance, surrender, and replay prevention need one adaptive lifecycle security proof.
why: Reproduction of scarce computational rights without treating scarcity as ordinary file access control.
key_works: Secure key leasing and certified deletion.

title: Quantum Chrysalis Leases — proposal
subfield: Quantum developmental cryptography
open: A holder replaces a protected capability for \(f\) with one for an approved \(f'\), without retaining unauthorized simultaneous use of both.
status: The proposal must be instantiated for a supported function class; arbitrary quantum program transformation is not assumed.
why: Upgradeable protected software whose licensing survives functional evolution.
key_works: Secure software leasing and quantum copy-protection of restricted programs.

title: One-Choice Reproductive Signatures — proposal
subfield: Quantum developmental cryptography
open: A quantum signing token permits one accepted birth message containing child identities, inherited policy, and resource allocation.
status: Token consumption must compose with birth registration and resistance to adversarially entangled attempts.
why: Scarce reproductive consent with publicly inspectable authorization.
key_works: Quantum tokens for digital signatures.

title: Selective-Inheritance Deletion — proposal
subfield: Quantum developmental cryptography
open: After deriving \(f(x)\), the residual adversarial view should reveal no more about \(x\) than the declared inheritance permits.
status: Deletion must compose with prior computation and auxiliary information; if \(f(x)\) reveals \(x\), nothing remains to protect.
why: Inheritance of useful knowledge without inheritance of an unrestricted dossier.
key_works: Certified deletion and everlasting-security transfer.

title: Deletion-Triggered Succession — proposal
subfield: Quantum developmental cryptography
open: Activation requires a valid deletion or surrender certificate for a protected predecessor capability, bound to the exact successor and epoch.
status: The transfer must remain safe under aborted handoffs, delayed certificates, and colluding predecessor–successor pairs.
why: Handoffs that establish cryptographic relinquishment rather than merely contractual promises not to keep using old keys.
key_works: Public-key encryption with secure key leasing.

title: Monogamous Knowledge Lineages — proposal
subfield: Quantum developmental cryptography
open: In a specified challenge game, separated descendant adversaries cannot exceed an allowed number of successful decryptions of the protected challenge information.
status: The research target is recursive delegation security; ordinary uncloneability does not automatically cover arbitrary interacting descendants.
why: Scarce knowledge rights that survive multiple generations of delegation.
key_works: Uncloneable encryption and its security limitations.

title: Noise-Tolerant Quantum Dormancy — proposal
subfield: Quantum developmental cryptography
open: Within a declared noise model, an encoded lease can be maintained and recovered while preserving its surrender and use restrictions.
status: Recovery information and maintenance access can change the adversary’s power; correctness under noise and leasing security need joint analysis.
why: Long-lived quantum capabilities that need not be continuously active.
key_works: Secure leasing and composable certified-deletion research.

title: Quantum-Share Organ Renewal — proposal
subfield: Quantum developmental cryptography
open: Security survives specified sequences of committee changes and breaches, even when the adversary eventually encounters many historical share holders.
status: Adaptive branching and recombination require a temporal access-structure theorem beyond a single sharing episode.
why: Distributed secrets whose long-term safety does not rest entirely on unverifiable classical erasure.
key_works: Secret sharing with certified deletion.

title: Reduction-Producing Cipher Seeds — proposal
subfield: Cryptography that generates cryptography
open: The output includes algorithms, security games, and a machine-checked reduction to explicitly named assumptions.
status: The seed cannot prove a hardness assumption true; the challenge is expressive synthesis with reliable reduction search.
why: Automated cryptographic invention for specialized environments without relying only on plausible-looking algorithms.
key_works: EasyCrypt’s mechanized cryptographic reasoning.

title: Security-Game Germination — proposal
subfield: Cryptography that generates cryptography
open: Generated games are linked to inherited games by checked implications or explicitly labeled separations, preventing silent weakening of the advertised target.
status: Useful game generation requires semantic reasoning about adversarial power, not merely renaming variables and oracles.
why: Protocol specifications that evolve alongside their applications.
key_works: EasyCrypt and universally composable security.

title: Assumption-Transparent Hybridization — proposal
subfield: Cryptography that generates cryptography
open: A hybrid carries a checked statement specifying whether security needs all constituent assumptions, any one, or a more structured condition.
status: Robust combination is primitive-specific; concatenating two constructions is not a general proof of “secure if either survives.”
why: Evolving cryptography whose resilience claims remain interpretable as its ingredients change.
key_works: Machine-checked cryptographic reductions and composable security.

title: Leakage-Typed Protocol Splicing — proposal
subfield: Cryptography that generates cryptography
open: Each component exposes a formal leakage interface; splicing must prove that combined observations stay inside the inherited disclosure contract.
status: Individually harmless outputs can jointly reveal a secret; the splice checker must reason about correlation.
why: Automated construction of privacy-preserving workflows from independently developed components.
key_works: UC composition and functional-encryption definitions.

title: Private Abstraction Discovery — proposal
subfield: Cryptography that generates cryptography
open: A generated abstraction must satisfy a checked simulation relation while revealing only the permitted abstract interface.
status: The abstraction must be useful and non-vacuous; “anything may happen” is sound but worthless.
why: Inspectable guarantees for complex private systems without publishing their implementation.
key_works: Relational program verification and functional commitments.

title: Witness-Encoding Metamorphosis — proposal
subfield: Cryptography that generates cryptography
open: Field encodings, bit decompositions, numerical formats, and witness layouts may evolve only with checked semantic correspondence.
status: Overflow, undefined behavior, and approximate arithmetic require different preservation relations.
why: Proof systems that optimize for changing hardware and workloads without numerical ambiguity becoming a security hole.
key_works: Verified compilation and updatable cryptography.

title: Parameter-Selection Autogenesis — proposal
subfield: Cryptography that generates cryptography
open: Parameter updates satisfy a declared concrete-security model and operational constraints, with assumptions and estimation methods carried forward.
status: A verified estimate is only as sound as its attack model; algorithmic certification cannot make an incomplete model complete.
why: Adaptive cryptographic infrastructure that does not depend on undocumented parameter tuning.
key_works: Mechanized game-based security proofs.

title: Cryptanalysis-Driven Primitive Evolution — proposal
subfield: Cryptography that generates cryptography
open: The system records the violated security claim, retires affected capabilities, and accepts a successor only with a fresh argument covering its new design.
status: Blocking one attack does not establish security; the successor still needs a meaningful game and reduction or clearly stated assumption.
why: Cryptographic infrastructure that can respond systematically to demonstrated failures.
key_works: EasyCrypt and cryptography with updates.

title: Non-Replayable Novelty Certificates — proposal
subfield: Evolutionary populations: selection, novelty, inheritance, extinction
open: Relative to a declared equivalence relation, a contribution proves nonmembership in the credited set without revealing its complete contents.
status: General semantic novelty is not efficiently decidable; the equivalence class must be restricted and explicit.
why: Open innovation markets with rewards for recognized new contributions rather than renamed copies.
key_works: ZK accumulators and authenticated set operations.

title: Cryptographic Heritability Trials — proposal
subfield: Evolutionary populations: selection, novelty, inheritance, extinction
open: Registered parent–offspring experiments prove prescribed randomization, mutation, evaluation, and statistical calculations across the enrolled sample.
status: The protocol must account for selection, missing offspring, and adaptive stopping rather than showing only successful families.
why: Reproducible evidence about whether agent and model improvements actually transfer to descendants.
key_works: Adaptive data-analysis validity and verifiable training.

title: Evaluation-Exposure Genes — proposal
subfield: Evolutionary populations: selection, novelty, inheritance, extinction
open: Spawning, merging, and renaming descendants do not reset a protected evaluator’s lineage-wide exposure accounting.
status: The accounting must include selection signals and side channels, not only explicit score queries.
why: Large evolutionary searches with meaningful limits on benchmark overfitting.
key_works: Adaptive holdout reuse and privacy odometers.

title: Blind Winner Propagation — proposal
subfield: Evolutionary populations: selection, novelty, inheritance, extinction
open: A private selection process certifies the winning rule and issues descendant capabilities while revealing only a prescribed selection output.
status: Repeated winner identities and reproduction patterns can disclose rankings even when scores remain hidden.
why: Evolutionary research in which competitive selection does not require publication of every design.
key_works: Function-hiding commitments and adaptive privacy composition.

title: Anti-Self-Dealing Fitness — proposal
subfield: Evolutionary populations: selection, novelty, inheritance, extinction
open: Fitness is computed from interactions satisfying authenticated independence, challenge-generation, and contribution rules within the enrolled identity model.
status: Distinct credentials do not imply genuinely independent people or interests; the enrollment assumptions must be explicit.
why: Evolutionary service economies resistant to obvious circular activity.
key_works: ZK graph predicates and private conservation mechanisms.

title: Proof-Bearing Niche Creation — proposal
subfield: Evolutionary populations: selection, novelty, inheritance, extinction
open: Each new niche refines or extends a committed task partition, with certificates showing how existing obligations map into the revised space.
status: Coverage measures must remain meaningful under refinement and cannot simply reward finer naming.
why: Open-ended autonomous research that can diversify without calling every change of subject progress.
key_works: Proof-carrying data and authenticated set operations.

title: Certified Extinction Boundaries — proposal
subfield: Evolutionary populations: selection, novelty, inheritance, extinction
open: Relative to a committed enrollment universe, extinction means all active capabilities are retired, expired, or assigned to explicitly limited posthumous executors.
status: This proves extinction of recognized authority, not disappearance of arbitrary software copies outside the system.
why: Verifiable shutdown of autonomous populations without publishing every historical member.
key_works: ZK set operations and private spend prevention.

title: Mutation Contribution Shares — proposal
subfield: Evolutionary populations: selection, novelty, inheritance, extinction
open: A committed attribution rule evaluates specified ablations or interventions and allocates a conserved reward across admitted mutations.
status: Attribution depends on the chosen experiment and interaction effects; it is not an objective measure of all intellectual contribution.
why: Collaborative evolution with inspectable credit assignment rather than ownership determined only by the final integrator.
key_works: Verifiable training and adaptive statistical validity.

title: Birth Before Beneficiary — proposal
subfield: Generative time: births, branches, promises, and unwritten futures
open: Genesis commits to a beneficiary-selection rule and inherited constraints; a future eligible party receives control through a certified activation.
status: The activation process must prevent selection manipulation and preserve availability without a permanent unrestricted custodian.
why: Endowments, scientific instruments, and services for communities or organizations that do not yet exist.
key_works: Functional commitments and dynamic secret sharing.

title: Counterfactual Descendants — proposal
subfield: Generative time: births, branches, promises, and unwritten futures
open: Counterfactual branches inherit a simulation state and restricted disclosure rights, while every external-effect capability remains unavailable.
status: The boundary must cover indirect effects through shared services, output channels, and later incorporation of branch results.
why: Autonomous planning through rich simulated lineages without uncontrolled real-world reproduction.
key_works: Capability attenuation and composable execution models.

title: Rejoining Timelines — proposal
subfield: Generative time: births, branches, promises, and unwritten futures
open: A merge proves reconciliation of state, authority, and external-effect records, explicitly identifying conflicts that cannot be undone.
status: Some conflicts are irreconcilable without compensation or changed guarantees; the protocol must expose rather than erase them.
why: Offline or partitioned autonomous organizations that can later recover a coherent shared identity.
key_works: ZK set reconciliation and exactly-once effect tracking.

title: Ancestral Bargains With Future Strangers — proposal
subfield: Generative time: births, branches, promises, and unwritten futures
open: Future contracts are generated within a committed bargaining envelope, and their execution cannot spend more authority or resources than the ancestor reserved.
status: The envelope must allow useful adaptation without becoming a universal authorization disguised as a template.
why: Long-horizon coordination without requiring present parties to predict every future counterparty or circumstance.
key_works: Functional commitments and contextual capabilities.

title: Computational Seasons — proposal
subfield: Generative time: births, branches, promises, and unwritten futures
open: Each season requires a prescribed sequential computation bound to a newly authenticated input; the guarantee concerns work ordering, not exact wall-clock duration.
status: Hardware variation and input withholding prevent treating sequential work as a universal physical clock.
why: Developmental schedules that cannot be accelerated merely by replaying an old seed.
key_works: Verifiable delay functions.

title: Obligation-Preserving Reincarnation — proposal
subfield: Generative time: births, branches, promises, and unwritten futures
open: Reincarnation creates a fresh lifetime identifier, inherits specified unresolved duties, and receives only newly authorized capabilities.
status: Identity continuity, liability continuity, and capability freshness must be separately specified.
why: Recovery and institutional revival without pretending a dead entity’s old permissions are valid again.
key_works: Private spend prevention and proof-carrying state histories.

title: Ancestry-Limited Exposure — proposal
subfield: Generative time: births, branches, promises, and unwritten futures
open: A current-state compromise exposes explicitly permitted lineage information but does not automatically reconstruct all earlier controllers, private states, or relationships.
status: Public outputs and retained auxiliary data may already link generations; the security game must include them.
why: Long-lived agents and communities whose historical privacy does not collapse under one future breach.
key_works: Proactive sharing and update-hiding ZK accumulators.

title: Commitments to Unwritten Futures — proposal
subfield: Generative time: births, branches, promises, and unwritten futures
open: Genesis commits to a generative policy, admissible future inputs, and expansion rules. Each later opening proves the unique or explicitly authorized expansion for the authenticated input history.
status: The missing foundation is adaptive binding and hiding for expanding object graphs—not ordinary commitment to a fixed string.
why: Open-ended cryptographic worlds whose inhabitants, rules, and artifacts emerge over time while remaining accountable to their origin.
key_works: Functional commitments, proof-carrying data, and cryptography with updates.
